editorial:
Imagine you are at a fancy dinner party with a rich family who thinks they have everything figured out. Everything is perfect until a mysterious guy named Inspector Goole walks in and drops a bomb on the table. He tells them a young girl just killed herself and asks if anyone knows her. At first, the family acts like they have no clue, but as the night goes on, you realize every single person in the room played a part in ruining that girl's life. It feels like a giant puzzle where the pieces slowly fit together, making you feel the tension rise with every single question the inspector asks.

The acting is top-notch and really sells the panic as the family's secrets leak out. You will love how the mystery unfolds, though some parts might feel a bit slow since it is mostly people talking in one room. If you like stories that make you think about right and wrong, you have to see this. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for the best picture, or maybe rent it on Apple TV if you are on a budget. Adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is also a great move if you love owning high-quality films.
endingExplained: After the inspector leaves, the family discovers that Goole might not even be a real policeman. They find out there is no such person on the police force and no girl died at the hospital. Just as they start to celebrate and feel safe, the phone rings. A real police officer calls to say a girl has just died and he is coming over to question them. It turns out the first man was a ghost or a warning from above.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves a good whodunnit with a moral twist.
